title: Research

Research Areas

1. Healthcare Regulation, Competition, and Organizational Behavior
This area examines how regulatory institutions and market competition shape organizational incentives, investment decisions, resource allocation, and performance in healthcare markets.
A central focus of my research is understanding when regulatory constraints meaningfully influence organizational behavior and when market incentives may dominate formal regulatory differences.

2. Healthcare Delivery, Organizational Change, and Access
This area examines how changes in healthcare organizations, infrastructure, and service delivery affect healthcare availability, utilization, and access, particularly in rural and underserved communities.

3. Healthcare Utilization, Care Settings, and Economic Evaluation
This area examines healthcare utilization, differences across care settings, and the economic implications of healthcare delivery and policy changes.
My research includes studies of inpatient, observation, and conventional outpatient care, as well as economic evaluation and evidence synthesis.

title: Research
text:
Methods and Analytical Expertise
My methodological background encompasses quantitative health services research, health economics, and health policy evaluation.
I use a range of statistical and econometric methods to examine healthcare policies, organizational behavior, and health service outcomes.
My methodological expertise includes:
Causal Inference and Policy Evaluation

Difference-in-Differences (DID)
Synthetic Control Methods (SCM)
Regression-Based Policy Evaluation
Additional training in Instrumental Variables (IV) and Propensity Score Matching (PSM)

Statistical Modeling and Data Analysis

Regression Analysis and Statistical Modeling
Longitudinal and Panel Data Analysis
Healthcare Administrative Data Analysis
Sensitivity and Robustness Analyses

Economic Evaluation and Evidence Synthesis

Cost-Effectiveness Analysis
Systematic Reviews and Evidence Synthesis

My research involves the construction and analysis of healthcare datasets, selection of appropriate comparison groups, assessment of identifying assumptions, and evaluation of the robustness of empirical findings.
Statistical Software: Stata, R

title: Huiwen (Casey) Zheng
text:
About Me
I am a PhD candidate in Health Services Research, specializing in health economics, at Texas A&M University.
My research examines how healthcare regulation, market structures, and public policies shape organizational behavior, resource allocation, and access to care. I am particularly interested in how regulatory constraints and market incentives influence the decisions and performance of healthcare organizations.
My current research focuses on hospital regulation, competition, and organizational responses to policy changes. I use causal inference and quasi-experimental methods, including difference-in-differences and synthetic control methods, to evaluate health policies and their consequences for healthcare organizations and communities.
Prior to my doctoral studies, I worked in regulatory policy and intelligence at Johnson & Johnson, Daiichi Sankyo, and Medtronic. This professional experience informs my broader interest in how regulatory environments influence economic decisions and organizational performance across healthcare and life sciences.
